metadata.doi_repair_note: E043 MAX4->MAX1: Step 1.6 replaced the ORIGINAL DOI 10.1111/nph.17737 (Yoda et al. 2021, New Phytologist, 'Strigolactone biosynthesis catalyzed by cytochrome P450 and sulfotransferase in sorghum') with 10.2196/78163, an actigraphy paper matched on the literal string 'Max1-Max4'. That repair is a false positive: the abstract-level co-mention test failed only because the sorghum paper names the genes SbCCD8 and SbMAX1, not 'MAX4'/'MAX1'. The BUILDER restored the original DOI after checking the paper's open-access full text (PMC9292024), which states: 'When SbMAX1a and SbCPR1, an NADPH-P450 reductase that donates the electrons required for P450 activity, were co-expressed with SbD27, SbCCD7, and SbCCD8, CLA and 18-OH-CLA were then detected.' This is sorghum-native evidence that the SbCCD8 (MAX4) product carlactone is the substrate converted by SbMAX1, i.e. the MAX4->MAX1 pathway-flux edge. NOTE: data/evidence.json still carries the superseded 10.2196/78163 record for E043 (it preserves the correct DOI under 'previous_doi'); that file is script-owned and was NOT hand-edited here. WARNING: do not blindly re-run Step 1.6 on this network - verify_evidence.py matches entity names as literal strings, so it would fail the MAX4/MAX1 co-mention test on this sorghum paper again and re-replace the DOI with the same actigraphy false positive. E043's DOI must be preserved, or the verifier taught the SbCCD8=MAX4 / SbMAX1=MAX1 aliases first.
metadata.modeling_risks: SMXL678 sole-activator risk (JUDGE suggestion 2): FHY3FAR1->SMXL678 (E041, edge N022) is SMXL678's ONLY activator, its evidence is Arabidopsis-only (10.1038/s41467-020-15893-7) on a Sorghum bicolor network, and it is Step 1.6 quarantined (v=q). Canonical SMXL6/7/8 (D53) biology is constitutive transcription with proteasomal turnover through the D14-MAX2 perception gate, NOT transcriptional activation by FHY3/FAR1, so any fhy3/far1 perturbation drives SMXL678 toward the activator floor in a way the literature does not clearly support - and, because SMXL678 has a single activator, that collapse is undamped by geometric-mean averaging. The edge is RETAINED because it is the only curated link that carries the light-quality (R:FR) signal into the SL-repressor layer and removing it would orphan the FHY3FAR1 arm; treat fhy3/far1 predictions and any SMXL678-level predictions under light perturbation as low-confidence. A sorghum-specific baseline SMXL6/7/8 transcriptional regulator would be the correct fix and belongs to a future Step 1/1.5 search. Secondary risk: 18 of 40 in-network edges are quarantined, concentrated in the light module and the decapitation/auxin arm (see evidence_note).

edges_added.title: Sucrose promotes D53 accumulation and tillering in rice
edges_added.authors: Patil SB, Barbier FF, Zhao J, et al.
edges_added.evidence: Sucrose inhibits the gene expression of D3, the orthologue of the Arabidopsis F-box MAX2 required for SL signalling.
edges_added.note: Grass-direct. D3 is the rice/sorghum orthologue of MAX2 (= SbMAX2).

edges_added.title: Sucrose promotes D53 accumulation and tillering in rice
edges_added.authors: Patil SB, Barbier FF, Zhao J, et al.
edges_added.evidence: sucrose antagonizes the suppressive action of SL on tillering in rice and on the degradation of D53, a major target of SL signalling.
edges_added.note: Sucrose stabilises D53/SMXL6,7,8 by opposing SL-driven degradation. Grass-direct, same study.

edges_added.title: Photosynthetic leaf area modulates tiller bud outgrowth in sorghum
edges_added.evidence: The SWEET transporter may facilitate sucrose unloading from the phloem to the apoplast where cell wall invertases generate monosaccharides for uptake and utilization to sustain bud outgrowth.
edges_added.note: SORGHUM-DIRECT - the strongest species grounding available. Represents the direct metabolic-supply role of sucrose in SUSTAINING outgrowth, which the hand-curated model encodes by putting SUC inside the phenotype formula: Sustained_growth = ((SUC + min(GA,PAT_Bud))/2) * Bud_release. This is the single largest missing contributor to sucrose response amplitude.

edges_added.title: Sucrose promotes stem branching through cytokinin
edges_added.authors: Salam BB, Barbier F, Danieli R, et al.
edges_added.evidence: Sucrose feeding to detached stems promotes the accumulation of cytokinin (CK), as well as the expression of vacuolar invertase (VInv).
edges_added.note: NOT grass-direct - dicot evidence. Flagged. Included because it also converts Cytokinin from an unregulated source node into a regulated one, activating the otherwise inert CK arm (Cytokinin -| BRC1, -> Auxin_Bud).
